the refund enters the `requires_action` status and Stripe emails your customer to request their bank information.

old_evidence.text: Disputes and chargebacks aren’t possible on credit card charges that are fully refunded.

findings: Both captures document the merchant creating a post-success Refund via API or Dashboard, Stripe using available balance and submitting to the customer's bank/issuer, and prior cancellation before completion. They retain original-destination, part/full amount and Connect charge-type boundaries.

The mapped summary has the general May rules but omits the November bank-debit overlap warning and the consequential requires_action workflow, and overgeneralizes cancellation, tracing and reversal details.
The reciprocal concept should route the new workflow, clarify dated dispute evidence, and retain the generic disputes and separate receipt documentation links.
substantive_changes: November adds a bank debit overlap warning for SEPA, Bacs, ACH, ACSS/Canadian PADs, AU BECS and NZ bank debits: merchant proactive refund plus a bank-initiated dispute can give the customer two credits. The guide routes to each payment method’s refund guidance.

November adds a Refund state and customer email workflow for some methods without native refunds, e.g. Konbini, PromptPay, Boleto and bank transfers. Creation/email requires_action, submission and processing pending, expected arrival succeeded, returned funds requires_action and another email for corrected details, no response by expiration failed, cancellation while requires_action canceled. `next_action` exposes type, email metadata and expiration. May described banking-information collection/cancellation in general.

November omits May’s fully-refunded credit card dispute sentence, alternate refund issuance from the payment details page and automatic/manual refund-receipt wording. Retain date and avoid inferring removal. November still describes cancellation from the payment details page and conditional refund notification email, which are distinct actions.

Replacing Node SDK examples with equivalent cURL requests, numbering/Markdown and editorial changes are presentational. API object/create and events links, action-section cross-reference and the added bank transfer refund link are navigation.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May-dated full-credit-card refund dispute language and details-page/receipt instructions. The November bank-debit warning addresses different payment methods and concurrent actions.

Preserve no-cost cancellation before completion, original processing fees not returned and possible refund fee, available-balance/insufficient-balance mechanics, original destination with issuer-handled expired-card fallback, and Connect direct versus destination/separate charge and transfer responsibility, including separate transfer reversal to recover funds.

Preserve Refund failure/cancellation attributes and `refund.failed`, PaymentIntent status distinction (processing is limited to US Bank Account in these guide captures), cancel uncaptured requires_capture instead of refund, and partner-specific reference availability and time limits.
conflicts: The May capture expressly says disputes and chargebacks are impossible for fully refunded credit card charges (old raw line 14); the November counterpart omits that sentence (new raw lines 13–17). Date the historical claim in source lines 21/70 and concept line 20, and preserve the separate partially refunded and pending-dispute paths. The omission alone does not establish changed policy.

Source and concept describe card refund cancellation too broadly and the bank-information flow too narrowly. Only some card refunds qualify for a short Dashboard window before reaching the customer, excluding charge reversals. The API or Dashboard can cancel applicable refunds while bank information is uncollected, and November's workflow names examples beyond bank transfers.

Source line 29 and concept line 28 generalize the 7-business-day and reversal conditions to all references. Both guides apply those particulars to ARN, which is conditional on partner support, and distinguish STAN/RRN fallbacks and selected local references.

Source line 25 and concept line 24 state lower IC+ network fees categorically. Both guides say reversals usually incur lower network fees and IC+ users might see a difference; refund itself might incur a fee and original processing fees are not returned.

Both captures use two timing anchors for return of failed refund funds: up to 30 days from the post date in failure handling and from the request in tracing. Do not turn the two sections into a single exact deadline. Both also say statement appearance depends on network/issuer and separately give approximate 5–10 business days for a refund credit.

The pending-refund dispute guidance is Stripe's recommendation to accept/challenge the dispute to avoid duplicate reimbursement, not a guarantee of duplicate credits. November separately warns of possible duplicate credits when a bank debit is proactively refunded concurrently with the customer's bank initiating a dispute.
unresolved_questions: The captures do not explain why the fully refunded credit-card dispute sentence and alternate Dashboard issuance/receipt guidance disappeared or establish current status from omission.
The two 30-day wording anchors are not reconciled by these captures. The approximate 5–10-business-day credit estimate is conditional and should not be treated as issuer settlement proof.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/refunds, both captures say a merchant can cancel before completion at no cost, refund part or all after success (potential fee and no return of original Stripe processing fees), and issue refunds through Dashboard or Refunds API within the original total. Stripe funds them from available balance, holds insufficiently funded card refunds pending and fails other methods in that case, then submits to the customer bank or issuer, with the original payment method as destination (old raw lines 8-26, old raw lines 83-89; new raw lines 9-27, new raw lines 74-80). For an uncaptured requires_capture charge cancel its PaymentIntent; Connect debits connected accounts on direct charges and the platform on destination/separate charges, with transfer reversal to recover (old raw lines 72-81; new raw lines 63-72). November adds the distinct Refund.requires_action flow for eligible methods without native refunds. Stripe emails for bank details, the customer responds and processing goes pending, expected arrival is succeeded, bank return prompts a repeat request, no response by expiry fails, and cancellation while requires_action yields canceled. Refund.next_action describes the request, addressee/time and expiry. May documents only the banking-information/cancellation prerequisite without the state table (old raw lines 127-135; new raw lines 122-166). source-stripe-refunds covers the May core and lacks this lifecycle and the bank-debit overlap warning.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/refunds, substantively update source-stripe-refunds for the November bank-debit double-credit risk when the merchant refunds while the bank initiates a dispute, and for the banking-information Refund state and retry workflow. May had the distinct pending-refund dispute recommendation and an older basic bank-details cancellation route (old raw lines 91-107, old raw lines 127-135; new raw lines 82-96, new raw lines 141-166). Date and retain the May statement limited to fully refunded credit-card charges and the alternate Dashboard issuance and receipt instructions, since November omits those passages while preserving conditional notification and payment-details cancellation (old raw lines 12-20, old raw line 37; new raw lines 13-21, new raw lines 29-40, new raw line 139). Preserve the eligible card cancellation exception for processed reversals and qualify ARN availability/timing and IC+ wording (old raw line 129, old raw lines 146-150, old raw lines 176-180; new raw line 124, new raw lines 168-172, new raw lines 198-202). Use the reciprocal stripe-refunds and the related disputes and receipts routes, plus new method-specific and bank transfer links. cURL replaces Node for the same API operations and link retargeting/numbering is navigational or presentational (old raw lines 45-72, old raw lines 244-256, old raw line 272; new raw lines 44-63, new raw lines 266-273, new raw line 289, new raw line 313).
